items_missed: Never asked for or used the customer's name once in a 10-minute call — she is a repeat Einstein customer and he still never said 'Stephanie'
No 'How are you today?' — went straight from greeting into the inquiry
No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation — jumped straight to collecting details
Never asked about additional rooms (storage unit, balcony, patio) in either apartment
Never asked whether they need packing services or packing materials
Never asked the stressor question ('anything you're particularly worried about with this move?')
Save Your Ass prep speech skipped entirely — no 'prep shortens the move,' no consolidation examples, no carload tip, on a move where two people are combining households
Disassembly/reassembly never mentioned even though a bed frame and desk are being moved
No sense-check after the clock explanation ('does that make sense?')
60¢/lb state coverage baseline never used to frame the $2,000 No Worries plan
Email described as containing 'all the information' but no mention of the bolded detail list at the top
Branch hours and how to reach us never given
Several garbled/misspoken lines — '$520,000 total,' 'the two and a half hour, hour $2 and a half hour minimum,' 'all three of these permits' — customer had to ask him to repeat the price at the end
top_strength: Handled a genuinely odd setup — two tenants on different floors merging into a third unit in the same building — by pausing to add the extra location in the system and then confirming all three unit numbers, and he was straight with her that this would land at the 2.5-hour minimum rather than padding it. Clean, confident close: offered the schedule, she took it.
coaching_note: Get her name and use it — a repeat customer went the whole call without being addressed once, and that's the cheapest warmth available. Second priority: the Save Your Ass prep speech was skipped entirely on a two-household consolidation move, which is exactly the job where a carload tip and consolidation advice keep the clock at the minimum he promised.
phone_presence_notes: Professional and reassuring on price, and closed warmly with 'hope you have a wonderful day,' but no name use, no 'how are you,' and long stretches of 'Okay. Okay. Okay.' filler make it read transactional rather than warm.
